message.content: {"summary":"An outstanding ethics report. You identified several ethical issues and linked them to engineering design, organisational context and stakeholders; built balanced, evidence-based arguments for and against shipping; and developed a defensible decision rule leading to justified multi-stakeholder recommendations. Your use of quantitative data and case studies (WannaCry/NHS, Therac-25, VW, Intel) was excellent, and your structure, tables, Figure 1 and referencing were all handled competently. Full marks across all criteria.","next_steps":["Strengthen the WannaCry analogy by acknowledging more explicitly that it evidences software vulnerability consequences rather than hardware defect rates, and consider pairing it with a hardware recall case (e.g. Intel Sandy Bridge or Takata) for a closer parallel.","Consider adding a sensitivity analysis or scenario table to Figure 1's decision rule, showing how the recommendation changes under different defect-severity or customer-type assumptions.","For future work at publication-level polish, standardise heading hierarchy and cross-reference numbering so tables and figures are cited consistently in the text."],"criteria":{"C1":"Excellent. You identified several ethical issues — test coverage driven by schedule, the data-loss rule and conflict of interest — and linked them to engineering design and organisational context. Table 1 comprehensively mapped stakeholder interests and decision control, demonstrating understanding of both context and stakeholders, which is what the top level requires. Sustain this tabular stakeholder mapping in future reports.","C2":"Excellent. Your for/against arguments were objective and developed in depth, each weighed per stakeholder (e.g. Stalk's time-based competition for shipping). You provided distinct decision-making recommendations for Rachel, management, the health department, the chip supplier and engineers — exactly the multi-stakeholder conclusions the Excellent level demands. Keep grounding arguments in evidence rather than opinion, as you did here.","C3":"Excellent. Your structure (for, against, decision rule, options, most ethical path) built logically to a well-supported conclusion, with Figure 1 and Table 2 systematically connecting arguments to recommendations for all stakeholders. Lines like 'it passes an unmeasured risk to the people least able to refuse it' show compelling, systematic reasoning. Maintain this argument-to-construction discipline in longer reports.","C4":"Excellent. Eight relevant references (NAO, Leveson, Stalk, Intel, DOJ, Engineers Australia, AS ISO 31000) combined quantitative evidence (81 of 236 trusts disrupted, 19,000 cancelled appointments, $4.3B VW penalties) with qualitative case studies (Therac-25, VW), supporting balanced, in-depth arguments. To push further, you could add independent corroboration for one or two key statistics.","C5":"Excellent. All required sections were present and functional; two tables and a decision-flowchart figure were used competently; prose was fluent, concise and accurate; and IEEE-style references were consistently formatted and relevant. Minor heading-level inconsistencies appear to be conversion artefacts and were not penalised. Continue using multiple visual element types as you did here."}}
message.reasoning: Produce JSON feedback. Full marks, outstanding. Summary ≤80 words, next_steps 3, criteria ≤70 words each.
